said.text: For too long, Washington has operated under a 'pay first, ask questions later' model that has allowed fraudsters to exploit government programs and steal billions from taxpayers. This legislation changes that by putting safeguards in place before money goes out the door.

did.text: Voted Yes on H.R. 8464, the Stopping Fraudulent Payments Act. Passed 218–200.

whyNote: The June 11 release hails House passage of an anti-fraud legislative package without naming individual bill numbers; H.R. 8464 was among the anti-fraud bills the House passed on June 10, and Rep. Langworthy voted yes on it.
